guard_streams.source: Pricing and consumer engagement 2025: interactive report

facts.detail: Ofcom published the 2025 pricing and consumer-engagement report on 26 February 2026.
The report covers fixed broadband, fixed voice, mobile, pay TV and subscription video-on-demand services.
It examines tariffs for bundled and standalone services.
It examines consumer engagement, switching, affordability and customer debt.
The publication provides an interactive report, a PDF and downloadable CSV data.

guard_streams.source: Statement: Network and Service Resilience Guidance

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the resilience-guidance page on 16 June 2026.
Ofcom states that resilient telecoms networks are vital to UK consumers and businesses.
The guidance covers architecture, design and operational practices that support robust networks and services.
The guidance sets out specific measures providers are expected to consider.
The main Guidance for Communications Providers on Network and Service Resilience is dated 16 June 2026.

guard_streams.source: Our network security and network resilience work

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated its network-security work overview on 12 May 2026.
Ofcom has had additional telecoms-security duties and powers since October 2022.
The duties arise under the Communications Act as amended by the Telecommunications Security Act 2021.
Public telecoms providers must take appropriate and proportionate measures to identify and reduce security-compromise risks.
Providers must also prepare for security compromises, including cyber-attack-related events.

facts.detail: Ofcom published its 2025-26 Annual Report and Accounts on 10 July 2026.
The report presents a long-term vision of pro-growth regulation enabled by competition, innovation and investment.
Ofcom says its long-term broadband framework will promote competition, innovation and investment.
The report highlights decisions enabling mobile networks and satellite companies to offer direct-to-device services.
It highlights plans to share spectrum across mobile and Wi-Fi services to improve wireless broadband and busy-location signals.

guard_streams.source: Moving landline phones to digital technology: what you need to know

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the digital-landline guidance on 19 February 2026.
BT plans to retire its PSTN by January 2027, requiring providers using that network to follow the same timetable.
Future landline calls will be delivered using Voice over Internet Protocol.
A digital phone needs battery or another backup solution to operate during a power cut.
Providers must offer a free emergency-calling resilience solution to customers who depend on their landline during a power cut.
